title: Frozen spec says edge cost = representative (lowest-slot) pipe's tier cost; code and canon docs implement MIN-member bundle pricing
detail: In a mixed-tier bundle whose lowest-slot pipe is not the cheapest (e.g. standard then wide), the spec prices the edge at 10, the code at 5. Decision-log and arch §6.2 agree with the code (min member). Spec wording is the outlier.
recommended_fix: Amend spec Changes §2 to "edge cost = MIN tier cost among live pipes toward the neighbor (the fattest member)" so the frozen spec matches decision-log, arch §6.2, and code.

title: cost ladder has no upper-bound validation; i32 dist sums could overflow with pathological data (documented + deferred)
evidence:
dist := make([]i32, int(n), context.temp_allocator)    // dist-to-dst per node slot (cost units)
---
				nd := dist[cur] + cat.pipe_tiers[t.pipe_tier[pi]].cost
---
  summary: Add an upper-bound validation for pipe_tiers cost (e.g. <= 1e6) to make dist-accumulation overflow impossible in routing_rebuild.
  evidence: catalog validation only enforces cost >= 1 (the ruling's per-hop progress guarantee); a pathological huge ladder value could overflow the i32 dist sums in the Dijkstra. The shipped ladder 20/10/5 is safe; magnitude caps on balance data are a pre-existing pattern (capacity_units etc. are unbounded too) — ride with the playtest/balance gate, not this canon job.
detail: Load validates only cost >= 1; no upper bound. An i32 dist overflow is only reachable with absurd ladder data, and deferred-work.md documents the deferred cap explicitly. Jobs B/C and ladder retuning build on this model.
recommended_fix: No change now: honor the deferred-work.md entry and add the upper-bound validation (cost <= 1e6) at the playtest/balance gate, before any ladder retuning.
